mainTopic: Defining a כרמלית and the public domain: the walled valley, the corner, the pillars and bench, obstacles in the street, and the size limits of a כרמלית
overview: This amud continues the ברייתא that lists places with the status of a כרמלית. רב אשי resolves the contradiction about a valley by saying the משנה means a walled valley. He is backed by עולא's own report from רבי יוחנן that a huge walled קרפף is a רשות היחיד by Torah law. The גמרא asks why עולא did not answer that way himself. עולא says a walled area would be called a קרפף, not a valley, and רב אשי points to the משנה's label 'רשות היחיד.' Next, the גמרא explains the extra item 'כרמלית' in the list as a corner beside the public domain, and it adds the area between the pillars and the bench in front of them, since their use is awkward. רב חסדא and others then discuss which raised or unpleasant spots in the street (a brick, thorns, filth) stop counting as רשות הרבים. Finally, רבי יוחנן and רב ששת set a כרמלית's size: at least four טפחים wide, and only up to ten טפחים high. The גמרא then begins asking what שמואל meant by 'above ten,' a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אשי: the valley in that משנה has walls
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי resolves the contradiction about the valley by saying the משנה that treats a valley as a private domain is talking about a valley surrounded by walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where it has walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב אשי's answer to an earlier contradiction. One source calls a valley a כרמלית, but a משנה treats a valley as a private domain. רב אשי says the משנה means a valley that has walls around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain open valley is a כרמלית. A valley fenced in by proper walls ten טפחים high is different, because walls are what make a רשות היחיד. So the two sources describe two different kinds of valley.

keyTerms.meaning: for example, as in the case of
walls or partitions (at least ten טפחים high)
a valley, an open field area
an in-between domain, neither fully private nor fully public, set up by the חכמים

phrases.english: For example, where it has partitions.
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי's answer, continued from the previous part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן דְּאִית לַהּ מְחִיצּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A valley is always a כרמלית, so a משנה calling it a private domain seems to contradict that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to a walled valley, which is a true רשות היחיד.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule on a huge walled enclosure supports עולא
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: a walled קרפף, even an enormous one not fenced for living, is a רשות היחיד by Torah law. Someone who throws an object into it from the public domain is חייב, because its walls are real walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: As עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a קרפף larger than בית סאתים that was not fenced in for living purposes, even if it is a כור or two כורים in size, one who throws into it is חייב. Why? It has a real wall. It is only missing residents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב אשי's answer with a rule that עולא himself reported from רבי יוחנן. Even a giant fenced area counts as a private domain by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים were strict about a large קרפף not fenced for living and forbade carrying in it. That strictness is only a rabbinic rule. By Torah law the walls still make it a full רשות היחיד, so throwing into it from the public domain makes one חייב. In the same way, a walled valley is a רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: an enclosed area, usually behind a house, used for storage
an area large enough to sow two סאה of seed (about 5,000 square אמות)
fenced in for the purpose of living there
a large measure, 30 סאה; here, a huge field area
one who throws an object (from the public domain)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle: a wall is a wall. Size and the lack of residents only bring in rabbinic restrictions. They do not cancel the Torah status of a רשות היחיד.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And like that which Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
An enclosure larger than two se'a of area
that was not fenced in for residence,
and even a kor, and even two kor in size,
one who throws into it is liable.
What is the reason?
It is a real partition,
except that it lacks residents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by showing that walls make even a huge area a private domain.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that a walled valley is a רשות היחיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule about a large קרפף

steps.title: Why didn't עולא follow his own קרפף teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why רב אשי did not follow עולא's answer. It asks why עולא did not answer with walls himself, since his own teaching from רבי יוחנן supports that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רב אשי did not explain like עולא. But why did עולא not explain according to his own teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two answers to the valley contradiction. It asks why עולא gave a different answer when his own קרפף teaching fits the walls answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי had his own reasons not to follow עולא's answer from earlier on the daf. But עולא himself reported that a walled area is a רשות היחיד by Torah law. So why did he not use that to explain the משנה as a walled valley?

keyTerms.meaning: like his teaching (here, like רב אשי's explanation)

steps.confusionAlert: 'כשמעתיה' here refers to עולא's own teaching, the קרפף rule he reported from רבי יוחנן. The question is why עולא did not use his own rule.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב אָשֵׁי לָא אָמַר כִּדְעוּלָּא,
phrases.english: Granted, Rav Ashi did not say like Ulla,
but Ulla, what is the reason
that he did not say like his own teaching?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב אָשֵׁי לָא אָמַר כִּדְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to compare עולא's answer with רב אשי's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did עולא not explain the משנה with his own קרפף teaching, as a walled valley?

steps.title: עולא's reason: a walled field would be called an enclosure, not a valley
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains why he did not use the walls answer. If the place had walls, the משנה would call it a קרפף, not a 'valley.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא could say to you: if it has walls, would the משנה call it a 'valley'? It is a קרפף!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains עולא's side. He rejects רב אשי's approach because of the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא agrees that a walled area is a רשות היחיד. He just does not think the משנה is describing one. The word 'valley' suggests an open, unwalled field, so reading walls into it (as רב אשי does) does not fit the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)

phrases.english: He could say to you:
If it has partitions,
would it call it a 'valley'?!
It is an enclosure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי דְּאִית לַהּ מְחִיצּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'בקעה' implies no walls, so the משנה's wording is the issue that divides the two approaches.

steps.title: רב אשי's reason: the משנה says 'private domain'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי, for his part, points to the משנה's own label 'רשות היחיד' to defend his reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי: the משנה teaches 'רשות היחיד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב אשי's side of the wording debate. He relies on the term 'רשות היחיד' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא builds on a different word in the משנה. One reading focuses on the word 'valley.' רב אשי focuses on the label 'רשות היחיד' and reads it in line with his own explanation. The debate ends as a standoff over wording.

keyTerms.meaning: it teaches (the wording of the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The valley contradiction has two answers. רב אשי says the valley had walls, backed by עולא's report of רבי יוחנן's קרפף rule. עולא keeps his different reading, since a walled area would be called a קרפף. Each defends his view from different wording in the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi: it teaches 'the private domain.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב אשי's matching reason, closing the comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי relies on the משנה's term 'רשות היחיד' to support his reading.

steps.title: Why list 'כרמלית' when every item is a כרמלית?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists 'and the כרמלית' among the כרמלית places. The גמרא asks why, since all the other items are already כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the כרמלית.' But aren't all the others also כרמלית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's list and challenges an item that seems to repeat the category itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the sea, the valley, and the colonnade as כרמלית, and then adds 'the כרמלית.' Listing the category as one of its own examples looks pointless. So this item must refer to some specific place.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: 'And the karmelit.'
Are all of them also
not karmelit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי לָאו כַּרְמְלִית נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves back to the ברייתא's list of כרמלית places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every item in the list is a כרמלית, so naming 'כרמלית' as an item adds nothing.

steps.title: It means a corner next to the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the extra item refers to a corner beside the public domain. People sometimes crowd into it, but it is awkward to use, so it is a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it was needed only for a corner next to the public domain. Even though crowds sometimes push into it, since using it is inconvenient, it is like a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word 'כרמלית' in the list points to a specific case: a corner beside a public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the corner counts as public domain because the public sometimes walks into it. רבי יוחנן says real public use must be comfortable and natural. Occasional crowding into an awkward corner does not make it public, so it is a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a principle for defining רשות הרבים: a place must be in comfortable, regular public use, not just entered now and then.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It was only needed
for a corner adjacent to the public domain.
For even though at times
the multitudes push and enter into it,
since its use is not convenient,
it is like a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the listed item as a specific case
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a corner next to the public domain, being awkward to use, is a כרמלית.

steps.title: The area between the pillars is a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, again through רב דימי, rules that the area between the pillars beside a public street is a כרמלית. People walk there, but they cannot walk straight through.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the area between the pillars is judged as a כרמלית. Why? Even though the public treads there, since they cannot walk through it directly, it is like a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ruling from רבי יוחנן. It follows the same idea as the corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spaces between pillars do get foot traffic. But the pillars break up the path, so people cannot walk freely and straight. Use that is not easy and direct does not make a place public, so it is a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: is judged as, has the status of

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Between the pillars is judged like a karmelit.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּדָרְסִי בַּהּ רַבִּים,
phrases.english: Even though the multitudes tread there,
since they cannot walk there directly,
it is like a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בֵּין הָעַמּוּדִין נִידּוֹן כְּכַרְמְלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same principle (awkward public use) to a new location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The space between the pillars is a כרמלית because people cannot walk through it directly.

steps.title: The bench in front of the pillars is a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports in the name of רב יהודה that the bench in front of the pillars is also a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב יהודה: the bench in front of the pillars is judged as a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more location to the list of כרמלית places: the merchants' bench in front of the pillars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Merchants placed their goods on this bench, and it is not a normal walkway. So it is not a public domain, and it is not walled off as a private domain. That leaves it as a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: a bench or platform where merchants place their goods
that is in front of the pillars

steps.whatToRemember: A place next to the public domain is only a true רשות הרבים if the public can use it comfortably and directly. A corner, the space between pillars, and the bench in front of the pillars are all כרמלית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Yehuda said:
The bench that is in front of the pillars
is judged like a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: אִיצְטְבָא שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הָעַמּוּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the pillar ruling to the bench in front of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bench in front of the pillars is a כרמלית.

steps.title: Comparing the pillars ruling and the bench ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the two previous rulings relate. Whoever holds the area between the pillars is a כרמלית certainly holds the bench is one. But whoever only said the bench might not agree about the pillars.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who said the area between the pillars is a כרמלית, the bench is certainly one too. According to the one who said the bench is a כרמלית, that may be only because a bench is awkward to use. The area between the pillars is easy to use, so it would not be a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the ruling of רבי יוחנן (pillars) with the ruling of רב יהודה (bench). It explains that one ruling includes the other, but the reverse may not be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bench is harder to use than the area between the pillars. So if even the easier-to-use pillars area is a כרמלית, the bench must be one too. But someone who only spoke about the bench may have meant that its awkward use is exactly why it is a כרמלית, so the pillars area, which is easy to use, would not be.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who said
All the more so (an obvious extension)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two places. The pillars area is EASY to use, and the bench is HARD to use. Being harder to use pushes a place toward being a כרמלית, not toward being a public domain.

phrases.english: According to the one who said 'between the pillars' (is a כרמלית),
all the more so the bench.
According to the one who said 'the bench' —
it is the bench whose use is not convenient,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּין הָעַמּוּדִים דְּנִיחָא תַּשְׁמִישְׁתֵּיהּ — לָא.
phrases.english: but between the pillars, whose use is convenient — not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בֵּין הָעַמּוּדִים, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אִיצְטְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes how the rulings in Steps 8 and 9 relate to each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pillars ruling includes the bench, but the bench ruling does not necessarily include the pillars, because the pillars area is easy to use.

steps.title: Another version: the pillars area counts as public domain
steps.stepSummary: A second version gives a different reason the bench ruling might not extend to the pillars. Crowds sometimes trample the pillars area, so it resembles רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: But the area between the pillars, which crowds sometimes trample, is like the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second wording of the previous point. This time the reason is that people sometimes walk through the pillars area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that the bench ruling does not have to cover the pillars area. They differ only in the reason. The first version says the pillars area is easy to use. The second says crowds actually step there at times, which makes it resemble רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Another version:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּין הָעַמּוּדִין דְּזִימְנִין דְּדָרְסִי לֵיהּ רַבִּים,
phrases.english: But between the pillars, which the crowds sometimes trample,
is like the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate reason for the second half of Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because crowds sometimes step there, the area between the pillars is like רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Throwing onto an upright brick in the street
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules about an object thrown in רשות הרבים at a brick standing upright. If it sticks to the brick's side, the thrower is liable. If it lands on top, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said in the name of רב חסדא: If a brick stands upright in the public domain, and someone throws an object that sticks to its side, he is liable. If it lands on top of it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. It shows that a spot in the street which people do not walk on is not treated as public domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side of the brick still counts as part of the public street, so landing there completes a forbidden throw of four אמות in רשות הרבים. The top of the brick is not walked on, so it does not count as public domain. Landing there is פטור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: how tall or how unpleasant must an obstacle be before people stop walking on it and it stops counting as public domain?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said in the name of Rav Chisda:
An upright brick in the public domain —
if he threw and it stuck to its side, he is liable.
On top of it — exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of which places count as public domain, depending on whether people walk there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Landing on the side of an upright brick in רשות הרבים makes the thrower liable. Landing on top of it is exempt.

steps.title: The brick must be three טפחים tall; thorns never count
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא limit רב חסדא's ruling to a brick at least three טפחים high, since people do not step on it. Thorns and bushes are excluded from the public domain even when they are lower than three.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both said: This is only when the brick is three טפחים high, so crowds do not step on it. But thorns and bushes are excluded even if they are not three טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא add a condition to רב חסדא's ruling. They also add that thorny ground is excluded no matter how low it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything lower than three טפחים is normally stepped on and stays part of the street. Thorns are different. People avoid them because they hurt, so even low thorns are not walked on and are not public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when (a condition)

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava both said:
And that is only when it is three (handbreadths) high,
so that the crowds do not step on it.
But thorns and bushes,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא גְּבִיהֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: even though they are not three high (are excluded).

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: וְהוּא שֶׁגְּבוֹהָה שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a height condition to רב חסדא's brick ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brick (or similar object) is separate from רשות הרבים only if it is at least three טפחים high, so people do not step on it. Places with thorns and bushes are excluded even when lower.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: thorns count as street, but filth does not
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב disagrees. Even low thorns and bushes stay part of the public domain, because people walk on them. A spot with filth, however, is not part of the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: Even thorns and bushes count as public domain. But filth does not.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion moves the line. It says thorns do not stop people from walking, but filth does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חייא בר רב holds that people will step on low thorns, so those spots remain public domain. Only something truly disgusting, like excrement, makes people avoid a spot completely.

phrases.english: And Chiyya bar Rav said:
Even thorns and bushes (are public domain),
but filth — not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ הִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי and רבא about thorns.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Low thorns and bushes remain part of רשות הרבים. A spot with filth does not.

steps.title: רב אשי: even filth stays part of the street
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי goes further. Even a spot with filth is public domain, since people in a rush step on it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: Even filth (counts as public domain).
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion pushes the line all the way. Nothing low on the ground removes a spot from the public domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי holds that busy people do not watch every step and will walk over even filth. So the spot stays part of רשות הרבים. This ends the dispute with three positions: thorns are excluded (אביי and רבא), only filth is excluded (חייא בר רב), or nothing low is excluded (רב אשי).
steps.whatToRemember: The key test for the public domain is whether people actually walk there. The three opinions disagree only about what makes people stop walking: thorns, filth, or only real height (three טפחים).

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said: Even filth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ צוֹאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step beyond חייא בר רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a spot with filth remains part of רשות הרבים.

steps.title: A כרמלית must be at least four טפחים wide
steps.stepSummary: Through רב דימי, רבי יוחנן rules that an area smaller than four by four טפחים cannot be a כרמלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה of the school of רב שילא said: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A כרמלית is not less than four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: the minimum size of a כרמלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny spot under four by four טפחים is too small to be its own domain. So it is not a כרמלית, even if it stands in or near a public area.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Of the school of רב שילא

phrases.english: Rabba of the school of Rav Sheila said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A karmelit is not less than four (handbreadths).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה דְּבֵי רַב שֵׁילָא: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule about the size of a כרמלית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An area smaller than four by four טפחים cannot be a כרמלית.

steps.title: רב ששת: a כרמלית extends up to ten
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds that a כרמלית 'extends up to ten' טפחים. Steps 18-20 work out what this means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: And it extends up to ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a short phrase to רבי יוחנן's rule. Its meaning is unclear, and this sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'up to ten' could be about height in the air, or it could be about needing walls ten טפחים high. The גמרא will now test what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: And it extends (takes hold) up to ten

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וְתוֹפֶסֶת עַד עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said: And it extends up to ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וְתוֹפֶסֶת עַד עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי יוחנן's size rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרמלית 'extends up to ten' טפחים (the meaning is clarified in step 20).

steps.title: What does 'up to ten' mean? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'extends up to ten' means. It suggests that a place is a כרמלית only if it has walls ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and it extends up to ten' mean? If you say it means that only when there is a ten-טפחים wall is it a כרמלית, and if not, it is not a כרמלית —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רב ששת's phrase and tries out one reading. This is a setup line: the next step will challenge this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reading treats 'ten' as a requirement for walls. Without a ten-טפחים wall around it, the area would not be a כרמלית at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposed reading, usually about to be rejected)

phrases.english: What is 'and it extends up to ten'?
If you say that if there is a partition of ten
then it is a karmelit,
and if not — it is not a karmelit,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְתוֹפֶסֶת עַד עֲשָׂרָה״? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב ששת's phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'extends up to ten' in רב ששת's statement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The proposed reading (walls of ten required) is challenged in step 19. The real answer comes in step 20.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's ruling about a low house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proposed reading with רב's ruling. Inside a house under ten טפחים, one may carry only four אמות, so it is a כרמלית even without ten-טפחים walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not a כרמלית? But רב גידל said in the name of רב חייא בר יוסף in the name of רב: A house whose inside is not ten טפחים high, but its roof brings it up to ten — on its roof one may carry everywhere, but inside it one may carry only four אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested meaning of 'up to ten' by quoting a ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the house, the walls are less than ten טפחים high, yet רב limits carrying there to four אמות. That is the rule of a כרמלית. So a place can be a כרמלית without ten-טפחים walls, which goes against the suggested reading.
steps.confusionAlert: The roof and the inside get opposite rules. The roof sits ten טפחים high, so it is a full רשות היחיד and one may carry everywhere. The inside is under ten, so it is only a כרמלית and one may carry just four אמות.

phrases.english: And is it not (a karmelit)?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Giddel say in the name of Rav Chiyya bar Yosef in the name of Rav:
A house whose inside is not ten (handbreadths high),
and its roofing completes it to ten —
on its roof, one may carry on all of it;

phrases.aramaic: בְּתוֹכוֹ — אֵין מִטַּלְטְלִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת!
phrases.english: inside it, one may carry only four cubits!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading proposed in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'up to ten' means a כרמלית needs ten-טפחים walls.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב treats the inside of a house with walls under ten טפחים as a כרמלית (carrying limited to four אמות). So ten-טפחים walls are not required for a כרמלית.

steps.title: New reading: a כרמלית exists only up to ten טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רב ששת's 'extends up to ten' as a height limit. A כרמלית exists only in the space up to ten טפחים, not above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'and extends up to ten' mean? It means that up to ten טפחים is where it is a כרמלית. Above ten טפחים it is not a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The first reading of רב ששת (walls of ten) was knocked down, so the גמרא offers a different meaning. 'Up to ten' describes how high the כרמלית goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'up to ten' is no longer about walls around the area. It is about the airspace above it. The space from the ground up to ten טפחים counts as כרמלית, and anything higher than ten is simply not כרמלית (it is a מקום פטור).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what [does it mean]? Signals a new explanation after the earlier one failed
Takes up / extends (how far the domain reaches)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two readings. The rejected reading said a כרמלית needs walls ten טפחים high. The new reading says the כרמלית itself only goes up to ten טפחים in height.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a vertical limit for a כרמלית, which differs from רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים, as the next steps will discuss.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'and extends up to ten' mean?
phrases.notes: Returns to רב ששת's words after the first reading was rejected

phrases.english: That up to ten [טפחים] is where it is a כרמלית;
above ten טפחים
it is not a כרמלית.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי ״וְתוֹפֶסֶת עַד עֲשָׂרָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that step 19 rejected with a new explanation of רב ששת's words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Extends up to ten' means the כרמלית exists only up to a height of ten טפחים; above that it is not a כרמלית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'extends up to ten' really mean, now that the walls reading has failed?

steps.title: שמואל's advice to רב יהודה about 'above ten'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the new reading to שמואל's advice to רב יהודה: do not get involved in שבת questions above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits what שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Sharp one, do not get involved in שבת matters above ten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar statement from שמואל that also treats 'above ten' as special for שבת. It backs up the idea that the rules change above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל calls רב יהודה 'שיננא' (sharp scholar) and tells him not to deal with שבת questions above ten. This matches רב ששת: above ten, the usual domain rules do not apply in the same way. The exact meaning of שמואל's words is still unclear, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: And like that which [someone] said; introduces a parallel statement
Sharp one / keen scholar (שמואל's nickname for רב יהודה)

phrases.english: And like that which he said to him,
שמואל to רב יהודה:
Sharp one, do not be [involved]
phrases.notes: שיננא is an affectionate title for a sharp student

phrases.english: in matters of שבת
above ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 20's height-limit reading with a parallel statement from שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that 'above ten טפחים' is treated differently for שבת domains.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's advice to רב יהודה not to get involved in שבת matters above ten.

steps.title: What did שמואל mean? A first suggestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law שמואל was talking about and suggests he meant there is no רשות היחיד above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law did שמואל say this? Should we say he meant that there is no רשות היחיד above ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what שמואל's statement actually means and offers a first guess. This sets up the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only said 'above ten' without explaining which rule he meant. The first guess is that רשות היחיד stops at ten טפחים, the same way a כרמלית does. This guess is put forward so it can be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (Which practical rule is meant?)
If you say… (introduces a suggested answer that is about to be tested)

steps.confusionAlert: The focus has moved from רב ששת's כרמלית to שמואל's statement. The guess here is about רשות היחיד, not כרמלית.

phrases.english: For what law [did he say this]?
If you say that there is no רשות היחיד
above ten?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the statement quoted in step 21 means, and offers a first answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific שבת law was שמואל referring to with 'above ten'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposed: that רשות היחיד does not extend above ten טפחים.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רשות היחיד reaches up to the sky
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is challenged by רב חסדא. If someone throws an object onto a pole in a רשות היחיד, he is liable even if the pole is a hundred אמות tall, because רשות היחיד extends up to the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חסדא said: If someone stuck a pole into the ground of a רשות היחיד, threw an object, and it landed on top of the pole, he is liable even if the pole is a hundred אמות high. This is because רשות היחיד goes up all the way to the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the guess from step 22. רב חסדא clearly holds that רשות היחיד does exist above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for throwing into a רשות היחיד means the top of the pole is still רשות היחיד, even far above ten טפחים. So רשות היחיד has no height limit. That means שמואל could not have meant 'there is no רשות היחיד above ten.'

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? Introduces a contradicting source
Stuck a pole/reed into the ground
Liable (here, for a forbidden transfer on שבת)
Rises up to the sky; has no height limit

steps.whatToRemember: רשות היחיד has no height limit; it 'rises to the sky.' A כרמלית, according to רב ששת, only goes up to ten טפחים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to look for a different meaning of שמואל's statement, since it cannot be about רשות היחיד ending at ten.

phrases.english: But didn't רב חסדא say:
If one stuck a pole in a רשות היחיד
and threw [an object] and it landed on top of it,
even if it is a hundred אמות tall, he is liable,
because רשות היחיד
rises up to the sky.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested meaning of שמואל offered in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that שמואל meant there is no רשות היחיד above ten טפחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא rules that throwing onto a pole a hundred אמות high in a רשות היחיד makes one liable, because רשות היחיד extends to the sky. So רשות היחיד clearly exists above ten, and the suggestion fails.
